title: In-process span forwarding shim and resilient header normalization
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Several internal services and third-party clients (older proxies, mobile SDKs, and lambda-style functions) either drop, rename, or fragment trace headers (W3C traceparent, B3, and custom Redwood headers). This causes broken spans, orphaned traces in downstream systems, and loss of latency/error attribution. We need an approach that: 1) normalizes incoming headers to a canonical in-process context; 2) forwards an in-process span context across worker threads/fibers and callback boundaries; and 3) provides a safe downgrade/fallback when headers are missing/corrupted to avoid noisy sampling explosions.

Scope: Implement a language-agnostic header normalization spec + shim implementations for Node and Go SDKs, add a lightweight middleware for edge proxies (ingress) to rewrite headers when we can detect legacy formats, and include a small runtime shim to forward spans across in-process async boundaries (fibers, goroutine-local, async_hooks). Also add tests, dashboards to validate efficacy, and a rollout plan with canary and metric-based rollback.

Design decisions and trade-offs: 1) Canonical format: use W3C traceparent internally as the authoritative trace id/span id pair, but carry legacy headers (b3, x-request-id) for compatibility. Trade-off: converting B3->W3C can mask sampling decisions; we will preserve sampling flags and add an explicit "x-rw-trace-source" tag for provenance. 2) Header mutation: prefer middleware at edge to minimize SDK complexity; however, some environments (embedded clients) can't be updated, so SDK-level normalization is required. 3) Span forwarding across async: implement a small runtime shim that uses async context (async_hooks in Node, context.Context propagation in Go) and a lightweight fiber-local fallback for frameworks that don't expose context. This adds complexity but avoids broken child spans in worker pools.

Acceptance criteria: 1) 98% of traces that previously lost parent spans now retain parent-child relationships in a 48h canary. 2) No more than 10% increase in sampling rate noise when fallback creates new traces. 3) End-to-end integration tests for Node and Go SDKs that simulate legacy headers. 4) Dashboards: new panel showing fraction of normalized headers, headers rewritten at ingress, and sample trace linkage rate.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Phase 1 (P0): Spec + middleware prototype. Deliverables: header-normalization-spec.md, edge middleware (Lua or envoy filter) to normalize headers.
- Phase 2 (P1): SDK shims (Node + Go) to: parse multiple header formats, map to internal traceparent, preserve sampling/provenance, and surface a simple API for explicit span forwarding.
- Phase 3 (P2): Instrument worker pool adapters (goroutines / JS worker threads) to forward context via shim.
- Phase 4 (P3): Observability: dashboards, alerts, and automated data checks.

Rollout plan: Canary on internal routing tier for 72h (5% traffic), monitor trace linkage and error budgets. If trace linkage improves and sampling noise <10%, expand to 25% then full. Halt if linkage degrades or error rate increases >3x baseline.

Monitoring & dashboards: New dashboard URL (internal) and metrics to track: normalized_headers_ratio, header_rewrite_count, orphaned_trace_rate, fallback_trace_creations, and sample_linkage_rate. We'll add trace sampling heatmaps to easily spot noisy clients.

Backward compatibility: keep legacy headers untouched when possible (pass-through), but annotate rewrites with "x-rw-trace-normalized: true" to help downstream debugging.

Docs & artifacts: design doc and test matrix linked below.

2025-03-13 - Liam Chen: Spike prototyped an envoy header normalization filter. Found b3 single-header entries that split into multiple headers; normalization logic needs to prefer W3C but retain b3 for legacy exporters.

2025-03-14 - Sofia Alvarez (Observability): Reviewed design. Request to include an explicit provenance tag and test for sampling preservation across conversions. Also requested dashboard showing top clients causing header fragmentation.

2025-03-16 - PR feedback (ENG): PR #542 added Node shim but tests failing on CI due to race in async_hooks context propagation. Suggested approach: add a microtask boundary flush for critical span handoff. See PR link in attachments.

2025-03-18 - Liam Chen: Implemented go/local-context fallback that uses context values with a small TTL for goroutine reuse. Load test shows ~1.8% p50 CPU increase on library init; acceptable for now. Added integration test simulating envoy rewriting.
